To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diversity of a bacterioplankton community is affected both by bottom-up (substrate composition) and top-down mechanisms (viruses).

(1) lytic viruses create niches within bacterial community, (2) these niches are occupied by bacteria that are adapted to the substrate composition and (3) the substrate composition is a major factor controlling community composition.

(1) the diversity of mixed bacterial cultures was influenced by the composition of the organic substrate and by lytic viruses and (2) the diversity of Gammaprotebacteria was not affected by the composition of organic substrate but by viral lysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of viruses in the control of diversity of marine bacterioplankton.
the effects of viral lysis on prokaryote communities and their diversity, and how these are affected by the composition of the substrate supply.
the effects of substrate composition and viral lysis on bacterial diversity in the context of marine planktonic systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system is complex.
the effects of the different factors are not additive but rather synergistic.
the diversity of a bacterial community is determined by a complex interplay of different factors, which can vary with time and space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
substrate composition is a key driver of bacterial diversity, while viral lysis is a key driver for richness and evenness.
viral lysis and substrate composition operate simultaneously to control bacterial diversity.
the bacterial community composition is mainly determined by the substrate composition, while richness and evenness are mainly controlled by viral lysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although viral control of bacterial diversity is important, it is only one factor in the complex web of interactions that shape the structure of marine prokaryote communities.
the effect of viruses on prokaryote communities is not limited to the reduction of diversity but also affects community composition.
the effect of viral lysis on diversity is not only dependent on the presence and activity of viruses but also on the substrate composition.
